content.text:
## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK

The spec is well-written and shows real engagement with repo conventions, but its streaming design contains a contract violation that the proposed test suite is structurally incapable of catching, its "permissive" chunk types are not permissive, tool-call correlation is unspecified (and under-budgets the duplication D6 authorises), and its four highest-risk wire judgement calls are simultaneously unverified, uncited, and walled off from the `extra_body` escape hatch that was supposed to de-risk them. Several factual claims about this codebase are wrong — most importantly that `ModelCapabilities` "informs the agent loop" (nothing in `paigasus-helikon-core` ever calls `.capabilities()`), and the release-plz mechanism cited in §13. Fix the blockers and roughly half the majors and this becomes a solid spec; the bones are good.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **§9 — `Usage` will arrive *after* `Finish`, violating the core event-ordering contract** — §9 states "final `usage` → `Usage { … }`, emitted immediately before `Finish`", which assumes usage and `finish_reason` co-arrive in one chunk. With `stream_options.include_usage: true` the real wire emits `finish_reason` on chunk *N* and then a **separate trailing chunk with `"choices": []` and `"usage": {...}`** before `data: [DONE]`. A per-chunk translator therefore emits `Finish` on chunk *N* and `Usage` on chunk *N+1*. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:63` says "`Finish` is the terminal event; nothing follows it." | Why it matters: any consumer that stops reading at `Finish` drops the only usage snapshot of the turn, and the agent loop's cross-turn summing (SMA-402) silently under-counts every LiteLLM turn. Worse, the reason this has never surfaced in the OpenAI provider is that its fixture is idealised — `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt:13` puts `usage` on the *same* chunk as `finish_reason`, which is not what OpenAI sends. §12.3's proposed "usage-then-finish ordering" test would be authored against the same fabricated fixture and pass against a broken implementation. | Suggested fix: buffer the finish reason and emit `Finish` only at `[DONE]`/EOF — the pattern already in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:73-87` (`translator.finish()`, called from `model.rs:150` and `:156`). Add a fixture in which the usage chunk *follows* the finish chunk with `"choices": []`, and assert `Finish` is the last event and `Usage` precedes it.

- **§9 — the "deliberately permissive" chunk types have three required fields** — the shown structs are `StreamChunk { choices: Vec<Choice>, usage: Option<Usage> }` and `Choice { index: u32, delta: Delta, finish_reason: Option<String> }`. `choices`, `index`, and `delta` are all mandatory for serde. Real proxied traffic omits `choices` on some LiteLLM error/keepalive frames, omits `index` on several OpenAI-compatible backends, and omits `delta` on usage-only trailing chunks. `ToolCallChunk` is referenced but never defined, and has no `index` field despite §9 saying deltas are "index-keyed". | Why it matters: one missing field fails `serde_json::from_str` for the whole chunk. Since the spec never says what happens to an unparseable frame, the implementer's choice determines whether the stream silently loses its entire finish/usage tail or dies — and the whole D2/§1.1 rationale is "leniency is a feature here". | Suggested fix: `#[serde(default)]` on every field including `choices`; `index: Option<u32>` (`#[serde(default)]`), `delta: Option<Delta>`; define `ToolCallChunk { index: Option<u32>, id: Option<String>, function: Option<FunctionChunk> }`; and specify warn-and-continue on an unparseable frame, matching `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/model.rs:159-169`.

- **§9 / D6 — streaming tool-call correlation is unspecified, and the state machine it needs is not in D6's duplication budget** — §9 says only "index-keyed; `name` on the first delta for a given index only, `None` thereafter", and §16 Q2 admits `index` may be absent. It never says what `call_id` to use when `id` arrives *after* the first `name`/`arguments` deltas for that index. That is the exact case the OpenAI provider needed a ~70-line pending-buffer machine plus four dedicated unit tests for — see `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:196-375` and the tests at `:402`, `:447`, `:484`, `:516`. D6 budgets duplicating only `to_chat_messages`; the translator is a larger and subtler copy the spec never mentions. | Why it matters: an implementer following §9 literally will drop tool names and argument fragments whenever the id arrives late, producing `Item::ToolCall { name: "" }` or an args JSON parse error in `ModelTurnAccumulator::finish` (`core/src/model.rs:519`). Fragmented `function.name` deltas (`"sea"` + `"rch"`) also need concatenation. | Suggested fix: specify the algorithm explicitly — buffer `name` and `args` per index until an `id` is observed, concatenate both, emit `name` exactly once per index — and list the four corresponding unit tests. Also decide the `index`-absent fallback now (correlate by `id`, else by position) rather than deferring to §16 Q2.

- **D4 / §7 / §7.1 / D11 — the two most uncertain wire decisions are unverifiable *and* have their escape hatch deliberately removed** — §7 nests `tags` under `metadata.tags` on the strength of an uncited claim about upstream docs, and sends `num_retries` as a body field while §16 Q3 openly admits this is unconfirmed ("if it is not, switch `.num_retries()` to emit the header instead"). Both keys, plus `metadata`, are in §7.1's reserved set, so `extra_body` cannot express the alternative — §15 states this outright ("`extra_body` cannot express the alternative (`tags` is reserved), which is a deliberate trade"). D11 removes live CI. Every proposed test in §12.1 is an `insta` snapshot of the crate's own serialisation. | Why it matters: there is **zero** verification, at any level, of any of the four LiteLLM-specific wire shapes that are the entire justification for this crate existing (§1.1 rationale #1). If `metadata.tags` or body-`num_retries` is wrong, the headline feature is a silent no-op in production, every test stays green, and the only workaround is a new release. | Suggested fix: (a) resolve §16 Q3 and the `tags` shape against a live proxy **before** GATE 1, not "at implementation time" — they are load-bearing decisions, not implementation details; and (b) remove `tags`, `num_retries`, and `metadata` from the reserved set so `extra_body` is a genuine escape hatch (document last-writer-wins, or merge caller keys *under* provider keys inside `metadata`); or (c) ship `.tags_top_level(bool)` and a header-mode toggle for `num_retries` so both alternatives are reachable without a release.

### MAJOR

- **§7 / §11 / D3 — "The capability flag informs the agent loop" is false in this codebase** — grepping `\.capabilities\(\)` across `crates/` returns only the provider crates themselves, `runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs` (pure forwarding on the decorator), and `cli/src/model.rs`. `paigasus-helikon-core` never calls it; there is no consumer in the agent loop. | Why it matters: §7 uses this claim to justify not sending `parallel_tool_calls` ("The capability flag informs the agent loop; it does not go on the wire"), and D3's whole conservative-defaults posture rests on the flags being acted upon. Both arguments evaporate. It also weakens §1.1 rationale #3 — a misleading `KNOWN_MODELS` hit can't mislead a loop that never reads it. | Suggested fix: restate D3/§11 honestly — capabilities are advisory metadata for application code and traces — and drop or re-argue §1.1 #3 (see below).

- **§1.1 rationale #3 is wrong as written** — "no table can be correct, and the OpenAI crate's `KNOWN_MODELS` lookup is actively misleading when pointed at a proxy." `capabilities::lookup` (`openai/src/capabilities.rs:154-160`) falls through to `conservative_defaults()` for unknown ids, and that function's doc comment (`:24-33`) explicitly names LiteLLM. The only failure mode is an operator alias that *collides* with a table id, and `OpenAiModelBuilder::with_capabilities` (`openai/src/builder.rs:97`) already overrides it — which is exactly what D3 proposes. | Why it matters: this is one third of the crate's stated justification and it does not survive a read of the code it criticises. Rationales #1 and #2 do hold (I verified the closed `FinishReason` enum at `openai/src/backend/chat.rs:264-274`). | Suggested fix: delete #3 or downgrade it to a footnote, and promote the genuinely correct third argument the spec buries in §9: `reasoning_content` has no representation in async-openai's stream delta types, so reasoning streaming through a proxy is *structurally impossible* via the OpenAI crate. Also note that SMA-451 mandates a crate, so §1.1's job is to justify the crate's *shape*, not its existence.

- **§10 — rows 2 and 6 contradict each other on connect-refused** — row 2 maps "HTTP 502/503/504, **or connect-refused**" → `Unavailable`; row 6 maps "`reqwest` transport failure" → `Transport(String)`. A connection refusal *is* a reqwest transport failure. | Why it matters: two engineers build two different error surfaces from the same table. Both variants are retryable (`runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:80-85`), so the bug is invisible in retry behaviour and visible only in what the user sees. | Suggested fix: delete "or connect-refused" from row 2. Gemini already settled this — `gemini/src/model.rs:118` yields `ModelError::Transport(e.to_string())` for send failures.

- **§10 — HTTP 500 is missing, making transient proxy failures non-retryable** — the table jumps from 429 to "502/503/504". Gemini maps `500 | 502 | 503 | 504 → Unavailable` (`gemini/src/error.rs:17`). LiteLLM returns 500 for `litellm.InternalServerError` and for many upstream failures. Under this spec 500 lands in `Other(anyhow)`, which `RetryPolicy::is_retryable` (`runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:80-85`) explicitly excludes. | Why it matters: a wrapped `RetryingModel` will not retry the single most common transient proxy failure, and the workspace's two REST providers will disagree about what a 500 means. | Suggested fix: add 500 to the `Unavailable` row; decide explicitly on 408 and 529.

- **§10 — the `context_length_exceeded` code match is too narrow for LiteLLM specifically** — the table checks `error.code == "context_length_exceeded"` (OpenAI's spelling) before falling back to a substring match. LiteLLM's mapped exception is `ContextWindowExceededError` and it commonly emits `context_window_exceeded`. | Why it matters: §10 explicitly argues the structured code is "the primary signal" and the substring match is "the fragile fallback" — but on LiteLLM the primary signal misses and every context overflow takes the fragile path, on the one provider whose error strings are prefixed and rewritten (`litellm.BadRequestError: …`). | Suggested fix: match `context_window_exceeded` and `context_length_exceeded` on both `error.code` and `error.type`.

- **§10 — 429 on LiteLLM is not always a rate limit** — budget/quota exhaustion (`ExceededBudget`, "Budget has been exceeded", virtual-key max-budget) also returns 429. | Why it matters: mapping it to `RateLimited` makes a wrapped `RetryingModel` burn its full attempt budget — honouring `Retry-After` sleeps — against a hard limit that will never clear. | Suggested fix: inspect `error.type`/`error.code` for a budget signal before the 429 → `RateLimited` default, and map budget exhaustion to `Refused { reason }` (non-retryable).

- **§7.1 — the reserved-key rejection is incoherent as justified, and impossible at the stated time** — the rationale is "we never let a caller's key override a field the provider computed **per-request**", but the check runs at `build()`, before any `ModelRequest` exists. Whether `tools`, `tool_choice`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `top_p`, and `max_tokens` appear at all is a per-request decision (§7 says each is "only when … is Some"). So the rejection is necessarily unconditional: `.extra_body(json!({"temperature": 0.2}))` fails at build even when no request would ever have set `temperature`. | Why it matters: the mechanism is stricter than its own justification and the spec doesn't acknowledge it, so an implementer may "fix" it by moving the check to request time and get a different, unspecified API. | Suggested fix: pick one and state it — either "unconditional, for determinism and a build-time error" (and delete the per-request wording), or move the collision check into request assembly and surface it as a `ModelError`. Separately, `.metadata("tags", …)` should fail as a distinct `BuildError::ReservedMetadataKey(String)`, not `ReservedExtraBodyKey` — the name lies about which builder method was misused.

- **§5 / §7 — `metadata` values are `String`-only, and the wire isn't** — `metadata(key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>)` cannot express LiteLLM's nested metadata (`spend_logs_metadata`, Langfuse `session_id`/`generation_name`, numeric values) — and because `metadata` is a reserved `extra_body` key there is no workaround at all. | Why it matters: D4 names "metadata/tags fit the repo's existing Langfuse observability story" as a justification for the crate, but the API is strictly less expressive than the field it exists to expose. (Note also that the repo's Langfuse story is OTLP-based — `crates/paigasus-helikon/examples/langfuse_tracing.rs` — and unrelated to LiteLLM request metadata; the claim is loose.) | Suggested fix: `metadata(key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<serde_json::Value>)`, and/or drop `metadata` from the reserved set with caller keys merged beneath the provider's.

- **§9 — multi-choice (`n > 1`) is unhandled and `n` is not reserved** — `choices: Vec<Choice>` with no rule for which index to honour. `n` is absent from §7.1's reserved set, so `.extra_body(json!({"n": 2}))` is legal. The obvious implementation is the OpenAI provider's `for choice in &chunk.choices` (`openai/src/backend/chat.rs:246`), which interleaves two independent completions into one `TokenDelta` stream and emits two `Finish` events. Gemini specced this explicitly ("Only `candidates[0]` is read; `candidates[1..]` are intentionally ignored"). | Why it matters: corrupted assistant text with no error, and a second `Finish` after the terminal one. | Suggested fix: honour only the first choice (or `index == 0`), document it in the crate docs, and add `n` to the reserved set.

- **§9 — no rule for a truncated stream (EOF with no `finish_reason`)** — the mapping table has no row for it. `ModelTurnAccumulator` initialises `finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop` (`core/src/model.rs:558`), so a stream that ends without `Finish` yields an apparently-successful `Stop` turn; a stream that fabricates `Finish::Stop` is worse. Gemini specified this and tested it (`gemini/src/stream.rs:73-76`, `gemini/tests/gemini_streaming.rs:60` `truncated_stream_no_finish`). | Why it matters: a proxy dropping the connection mid-generation is indistinguishable from a clean completion; the truncated text is committed to session history as final. | Suggested fix: state "emit `Finish` only when a `finish_reason` was observed; on premature EOF end the stream without `Finish`" and add the test.

- **§6.1 — base-URL normalisation is lossy, irreversible, and its algorithm is unspecified** — three separate problems. (1) The trailing-`/v1` strip is unconditional with no override, so a gateway genuinely mounted under a path ending in `v1` is unreachable and there is no `.endpoint_path()`/`.chat_completions_path()` escape. (2) The spec describes string operations ("trim a trailing `/`, strip a trailing `/v1`, then append") but validates with `reqwest::Url::parse` — if the ops are string-level, `http://gw/litellm?key=x` becomes `http://gw/litellm?key=x/v1/chat/completions`. (3) `Url::parse` will not catch the most likely typo: `Url::parse("localhost:4000")` **succeeds** (scheme `localhost`, path `4000`), so `InvalidBaseUrl` gives false confidence. | Why it matters: D7 argues a build error beats silently targeting the wrong endpoint — but as specified, the validation admits the classic scheme-less typo and the normalisation can silently mangle a legitimate URL. | Suggested fix: normalise via `Url` (`path_segments_mut`), reject schemes other than `http`/`https` and reject a non-empty query or fragment, and add an explicit path override for gateways the heuristic gets wrong.

- **§12.2 — the "`Authorization` absent" test as specified passes against a broken implementation** — wiremock has no negative header matcher; a `Mock::given(method("POST"))` with no header condition matches whether or not the header was sent. The only correct form is capturing `server.received_requests().await` and asserting the key is absent from the recorded request. | Why it matters: this is the *security-relevant* assertion for D8 (optional auth), and as written it is vacuous. It is precisely the failure mode called out in this repo's own review history: a security test that would pass against vulnerable code. | Suggested fix: specify the `received_requests()` form, and mutation-check it — temporarily emit the header and confirm the test fails.

- **D6 / §15 R1 — the stated mitigation cannot detect the risk it claims to mitigate, and the duplication is under-counted** — R1 says drift is caught because "snapshot tests pin **this crate's** shape so drift is visible". A snapshot of crate B tells you nothing about crate A; both suites stay green while the two mappings diverge arbitrarily. And D6 accounts only for `to_chat_messages` (~120 lines, `openai/src/translate/request.rs:26-243`); the real copy is that plus `ChatTranslator` (~170 lines, `backend/chat.rs:196-375`), `translate_tool_choice` (`:181-194`), and `to_openai_response_format`. Meanwhile D6's stated cost of the alternative — "the same-PR core/facade bump ritual" — is a ~5-line Cargo.toml edit that CLAUDE.md documents step by step, and its second rationale ("the two mappings should be free to diverge") is close to self-refuting: LiteLLM's chat surface *is* the OpenAI Chat surface; divergence means LiteLLM stopped being OpenAI-compatible. | Why it matters: ~350 lines of subtle, already-battle-tested logic get re-derived without tests carried over, justified by a cost that is trivial and a benefit that is hypothetical. | Suggested fix: either hoist to `paigasus_helikon_core::wire::openai_chat` and pay the documented core+facade bump, or keep the copy and (a) port the OpenAI crate's unit tests verbatim alongside the copied functions so behavioural parity is pinned at copy time, and (b) add a real cross-crate parity test (facade test dir, both features on, shared fixture set asserted byte-identical). Update R1 to say which.

- **D5 — throwing away `x-litellm-*` leaves the crate with no correlation story, and the justification only covers half the problem** — D5 is correct that `ModelEvent` has no header carrier (verified: `core/src/model.rs:168-224`). But nothing prevents the provider from `tracing::debug!`-ing `x-litellm-call-id` / `x-litellm-model-id` on response receipt and attaching them to `ModelError::Other`'s anyhow context on failure. | Why it matters: this is a provider whose entire purpose is being a routing and observability chokepoint. As specified, a user with a failing call has no way to find it in LiteLLM's own logs — and §15 already accepts that capability mis-declaration and fallback surprises "surface as an upstream 400 mapped to `Other`", which is exactly the error the call-id would explain. Zero core change required. | Suggested fix: log the correlation headers at `debug` and include `x-litellm-call-id` in the error context for every non-2xx path. Narrow D5 to "not surfaced as a typed API".

- **§13 / packaging — the release-plz mechanism cited is the wrong one** — §13 says "release-plz's `dependencies_update` cascade handles the facade on its own." That cascade fires only when release-plz *itself* bumps a sibling. Here the new crate is authored at `0.1.0` by the PR, so release-plz never bumps it — this is exactly the "same-PR manual bump silently defeats `dependencies_update`" case CLAUDE.md documents. The facade gets bumped only by **path attribution** on the squashed commit touching `crates/paigasus-helikon/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`, which requires the squashed PR title to be `feat`/`fix`. | Why it matters: a `chore(...)`-titled squash merge would publish the new crate and leave the facade at `0.5.3` with no `litellm` feature — the exact drift that needed follow-up PR #50 after SMA-346. | Suggested fix: replace the claim with the Gemini spec's correct wording (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-sma-449-gemini-provider-design.md:433-436` — dependency-ordered publish, new crate depends only on already-published core, first publish is clean), and add an explicit constraint that the PR title must be `feat(providers): …`.

- **Packaging — the commit/PR-title scope is unspecified and the obvious guess breaks CI** — `providers-litellm` is absent from `.versionrc:18` (`scopeRegex`) and from `pr-title.yml:43-75` (`scopes`), as are `providers-gemini` and `providers-bedrock`. `feat(providers-litellm): …` is rejected by the local `commit-msg` hook and by the `commits` job. Because `pr-title.yml` runs on `pull_request_target`, the allowlist is read from `main`, so this PR cannot register a new scope and then use it in its own title. | Why it matters: a guaranteed red required check, discovered at push time, on a spec that otherwise documents CI conventions carefully. | Suggested fix: state that all commits and the PR title use scope `providers` (or `facade` for the wiring commit), and note the `pull_request_target` reason so nobody "fixes" it by editing the allowlist.

### MINOR

- **§14 — the documentation plan under-counts the pages that go stale.** `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md` says "Four adapters ship today" at **line 6 and again at line 85**, has a "Switching providers is one line" code block at **305-317** and an "Enabling the providers" toml at **334-343** — all four need editing. `docs/book/src/getting-started/workspace-layout.md:56-57` carries the crate list and is **not mentioned at all** in §14. `docs/book/src/reference/crates.md` needs *two* rows (roster ~line 27 **and** the feature→module map ~line 57), not one. Root `README.md:29` and `:38` both enumerate providers. Fix: enumerate these explicitly so nothing is skipped.

- **§11 — `.with_capabilities()` can produce a self-contradictory model.** An operator passing `ModelCapabilities::empty().with_tools()` sets `streaming: false` on a provider that has no non-streaming path (§3 out-of-scope: "The provider always streams"). Fix: force `streaming = true` after applying the override, or document that `streaming` is ignored.

- **§11 vs §8/§9/§12.1 — the default capability set contradicts the implemented feature set.** `conservative_defaults()` sets only `streaming|tools`, yet the crate emits `ReasoningDelta` (§9), maps `response_format` (§8), and snapshots an inline image part (§12.1) — so `reasoning`, `structured_output`, and `vision` are all `false` while implemented. §9's flourish ("this provider gets reasoning streaming that the Gemini provider still lacks") reads as contradicting §11. Fix: state explicitly that the flags describe the *unknown proxied backend*, not the translator's ability.

- **§5 / D7 — env var names are uncited and have no fallback.** `LITELLM_API_BASE` / `LITELLM_API_KEY` are asserted with no source; LiteLLM's own client conventions also use `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE` / `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY`. D7's "a loud build error beats silently targeting localhost" argument depends on operators having exported the exact name this crate expects. Gemini set the precedent for a documented fallback chain (`gemini/src/model.rs:46-48`). Fix: cite the source or add the `LITELLM_PROXY_*` fallback.

- **D8 / §6.2 — empty/whitespace API key is unhandled.** `.api_key("")` yields `Authorization: Bearer ` — a malformed header reqwest will happily send and LiteLLM will 401 on, which D8's "loud 401" framing then misattributes to a misconfigured *deployment*. Gemini has an explicit `EmptyApiKey`. Fix: treat empty/whitespace as absent, or add the variant.

- **§7/§8 — `ToolChoice::Required` / `Tool { name }` with empty `request.tools` is silently dropped.** §7 sends `tool_choice` "only when `ModelSettings.tool_choice` is `Some` AND `request.tools` is non-empty". The caller who set `Required` believes a tool call is guaranteed. Gemini errors on this case. Fix: at minimum `tracing::warn!`; ideally mirror Gemini and error.

- **§7 — the `drop_params` argument is applied to `parallel_tool_calls` but not to `max_tokens`.** §7 declines to send `parallel_tool_calls: false` because "LiteLLM only strips unknown params when the operator sets `drop_params`" — then unconditionally sends `max_tokens`, which OpenAI's o-series and gpt-5 reject in favour of `max_completion_tokens`, hitting exactly the same failure mode. Fix: state the decision explicitly (send `max_tokens`, or branch, or document the `drop_params` requirement) so the reasoning is consistent across adjacent fields.

- **§5 — no `Send`/`'static` story for the model's state.** §5 shows a bare `pub struct LiteLlmModel { /* … */ }`; `Model::invoke` returns `BoxStream<'static, …>` (`core/src/model.rs:72`), so the config must be cloned into the stream. Gemini solves it with `GeminiModel(Arc<Config>)` + `#[derive(Clone)]` (`gemini/src/model.rs:22-23`) precisely for this reason. Fix: state the `Arc<Config>` shape.

- **No timeout policy and no secret-redaction policy.** `reqwest::Client::new()` has no default timeout, so a hung self-hosted proxy hangs `invoke` indefinitely with cancellation as the only out — a higher-probability failure for an operator-run gateway than for a hyperscaler. Separately, if `Config`/`Builder` derive `Debug` with the key inline (as Gemini's `Auth::ApiKey(String)` does), `{model:?}` leaks the key; `extra_body` is arbitrary caller JSON that the §12.1 snapshots serialise wholesale. Fix: specify a `connect_timeout` default (or document that callers must supply `.http_client()`), a manual redacting `Debug`, and that no `tracing` event logs the `Authorization` header or a full request body.

- **§16 Q1 is already answered in-tree.** "Confirm `eventsource-stream` yields `[DONE]` as an ordinary `data` event" — `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/model.rs:155` does `if event.data == "[DONE]" { … return; }` and ships. Fix: cite the precedent and remove Q1 from the open list.

- **§12.4 "cancel mid-stream" is close to untestable with the stated harness.** Wiremock serves the whole body in one `set_body_raw` — the header comment on `openai/tests/chat_streaming.rs:3` says so outright ("Wiremock serves the entire fixture as one buffer — these tests prove byte-level correctness of the translator's state machine, not pacing"). The OpenAI crate only tests cancel-*before*-first-chunk (`tests/cancellation.rs:22`). Fix: either drop the mid-stream case or specify the mechanism (`set_delay` plus a multi-response mock sequence).

- **Missing tests for stated invariants.** No test that `parallel_tool_calls` is absent from the body (§7 invariant); no test that `previous_response_id` is never sent (§7); no test that the reserved-key set is *exhaustive* with respect to the serialiser. Fix: add a test that iterates the `RESERVED` const against a maximally-populated request body and asserts every emitted top-level key is reserved — this is the test that catches "we added `seed` to the body and forgot to reserve it".

- **§13 — no crates.io name preflight.** The Gemini spec carried a name-claim AC. Note that per this repo's history the crates.io API 403s the default curl User-Agent, so a naive availability check reads as unavailable. Fix: preflight `paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm` with a custom UA before GATE 1.

### QUESTIONS

- Is `classify()` a pure function taking `(status, code, type, message, retry_after_ms)`, as Gemini's is (`gemini/src/error.rs:9`)? §12.5's "one error-mapping test per row" is only cheap if it is; §10 never says.
- Do errors surface as `Err` returned from `invoke`, or as the first `Err` item on the returned stream? Gemini does the latter (`gemini/src/model.rs:136`); D8's "loud 401 → `ModelError::Refused` on first invoke" reads like the former. `RetryingModel` handles both (`runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:190`, `:234`), but call-site code differs.
- What happens to an SSE frame that fails to deserialise — warn-and-continue (Gemini) or terminate? And what happens to an `error` frame that arrives *after* a `Finish` has been emitted?
- Is `delta.reasoning_content` the only reasoning field? Some LiteLLM builds emit `delta.reasoning` and/or `delta.thinking_blocks` depending on backend and version. Does §9 want a fallback chain, and does the answer change the `ReasoningDelta` mapping?
- What is the documented interaction between LiteLLM's server-side `num_retries`/`fallbacks` and a client-side `RetryingModel`? Attempts multiply (N_client × N_server) and each client retry re-runs the entire fallback chain, so a `RetryPolicy::new()` (3 attempts) around `.num_retries(2)` plus two fallbacks is up to 18 upstream calls per turn. Should the crate docs warn, or should `.num_retries()` be documented as mutually exclusive with `RetryingModel`?
- Is there an empty-conversation guard? OpenAI Chat 400s on `messages: []`, and Gemini specced an explicit early `ModelError` for it. Is "let it 400 upstream" the deliberate choice here?
- Does `Usage` really arrive exactly once? §9 asserts "One terminal snapshot satisfies core's cumulative-within-turn / last-wins contract trivially" — but several LiteLLM backends emit per-chunk usage. Last-wins still holds if the values are cumulative; it breaks if any backend emits per-chunk *deltas* (`core/src/model.rs:198-204` says such a provider would under-count). Has this been checked?

## What's good

- **§1.1 is genuinely rigorous** and rare: it starts by arguing against its own existence, names the exact prior art with a file:line, and two of its three arguments survive verification — the closed `FinishReason` enum is real (`openai/src/backend/chat.rs:264-274`, with the code's own comment noting the enum is not `#[non_exhaustive]`), and `base_url()`'s LiteLLM doc comment is exactly where the spec says it is (`openai/src/builder.rs:72`). Keep this section's posture; just fix rationale #3.
- **Every field of `ModelSettings` is accounted for**, including an explicit and correct decision on `previous_response_id` (§7) — checked against `core/src/model.rs:134-154`. Provider specs routinely leave a field unmapped and undiscussed; this one doesn't.
- **Dependency hygiene is exact.** Every crate listed in §13 exists in root `[workspace.dependencies]` at the right feature set, matching `providers-gemini/Cargo.toml:17-38` line for line, and **no new third-party crate is introduced** — so no new licence, advisory, or rustls-`CryptoProvider` surface. Together with the `.gitattributes` rule, the facade `///`-on-`pub use` note, and the `-D warnings` docs-job note, this shows CLAUDE.md was read rather than skimmed.
- **D9's instinct — never silently drop a caller's key — is right**, even though the mechanism needs rework. Preserve the principle when reworking §7.1.

## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK

The spec is well-written and shows real engagement with repo conventions, but its streaming design contains a contract violation that the proposed test suite is structurally incapable of catching, its "permissive" chunk types are not permissive, tool-call correlation is unspecified (and under-budgets the duplication D6 authorises), and its four highest-risk wire judgement calls are simultaneously unverified, uncited, and walled off from the `extra_body` escape hatch that was supposed to de-risk them. Several factual claims about this codebase are wrong — most importantly that `ModelCapabilities` "informs the agent loop" (nothing in `paigasus-helikon-core` ever calls `.capabilities()`), and the release-plz mechanism cited in §13. Fix the blockers and roughly half the majors and this becomes a solid spec; the bones are good.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **§9 — `Usage` will arrive *after* `Finish`, violating the core event-ordering contract** — §9 states "final `usage` → `Usage { … }`, emitted immediately before `Finish`", which assumes usage and `finish_reason` co-arrive in one chunk. With `stream_options.include_usage: true` the real wire emits `finish_reason` on chunk *N* and then a **separate trailing chunk with `"choices": []` and `"usage": {...}`** before `data: [DONE]`. A per-chunk translator therefore emits `Finish` on chunk *N* and `Usage` on chunk *N+1*. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:63` says "`Finish` is the terminal event; nothing follows it." | Why it matters: any consumer that stops reading at `Finish` drops the only usage snapshot of the turn, and the agent loop's cross-turn summing (SMA-402) silently under-counts every LiteLLM turn. Worse, the reason this has never surfaced in the OpenAI provider is that its fixture is idealised — `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt:13` puts `usage` on the *same* chunk as `finish_reason`, which is not what OpenAI sends. §12.3's proposed "usage-then-finish ordering" test would be authored against the same fabricated fixture and pass against a broken implementation. | Suggested fix: buffer the finish reason and emit `Finish` only at `[DONE]`/EOF — the pattern already in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:73-87` (`translator.finish()`, called from `model.rs:150` and `:156`). Add a fixture in which the usage chunk *follows* the finish chunk with `"choices": []`, and assert `Finish` is the last event and `Usage` precedes it.

- **§9 — the "deliberately permissive" chunk types have three required fields** — the shown structs are `StreamChunk { choices: Vec<Choice>, usage: Option<Usage> }` and `Choice { index: u32, delta: Delta, finish_reason: Option<String> }`. `choices`, `index`, and `delta` are all mandatory for serde. Real proxied traffic omits `choices` on some LiteLLM error/keepalive frames, omits `index` on several OpenAI-compatible backends, and omits `delta` on usage-only trailing chunks. `ToolCallChunk` is referenced but never defined, and has no `index` field despite §9 saying deltas are "index-keyed". | Why it matters: one missing field fails `serde_json::from_str` for the whole chunk. Since the spec never says what happens to an unparseable frame, the implementer's choice determines whether the stream silently loses its entire finish/usage tail or dies — and the whole D2/§1.1 rationale is "leniency is a feature here". | Suggested fix: `#[serde(default)]` on every field including `choices`; `index: Option<u32>` (`#[serde(default)]`), `delta: Option<Delta>`; define `ToolCallChunk { index: Option<u32>, id: Option<String>, function: Option<FunctionChunk> }`; and specify warn-and-continue on an unparseable frame, matching `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/model.rs:159-169`.

- **§9 / D6 — streaming tool-call correlation is unspecified, and the state machine it needs is not in D6's duplication budget** — §9 says only "index-keyed; `name` on the first delta for a given index only, `None` thereafter", and §16 Q2 admits `index` may be absent. It never says what `call_id` to use when `id` arrives *after* the first `name`/`arguments` deltas for that index. That is the exact case the OpenAI provider needed a ~70-line pending-buffer machine plus four dedicated unit tests for — see `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:196-375` and the tests at `:402`, `:447`, `:484`, `:516`. D6 budgets duplicating only `to_chat_messages`; the translator is a larger and subtler copy the spec never mentions. | Why it matters: an implementer following §9 literally will drop tool names and argument fragments whenever the id arrives late, producing `Item::ToolCall { name: "" }` or an args JSON parse error in `ModelTurnAccumulator::finish` (`core/src/model.rs:519`). Fragmented `function.name` deltas (`"sea"` + `"rch"`) also need concatenation. | Suggested fix: specify the algorithm explicitly — buffer `name` and `args` per index until an `id` is observed, concatenate both, emit `name` exactly once per index — and list the four corresponding unit tests. Also decide the `index`-absent fallback now (correlate by `id`, else by position) rather than deferring to §16 Q2.

- **D4 / §7 / §7.1 / D11 — the two most uncertain wire decisions are unverifiable *and* have their escape hatch deliberately removed** — §7 nests `tags` under `metadata.tags` on the strength of an uncited claim about upstream docs, and sends `num_retries` as a body field while §16 Q3 openly admits this is unconfirmed ("if it is not, switch `.num_retries()` to emit the header instead"). Both keys, plus `metadata`, are in §7.1's reserved set, so `extra_body` cannot express the alternative — §15 states this outright ("`extra_body` cannot express the alternative (`tags` is reserved), which is a deliberate trade"). D11 removes live CI. Every proposed test in §12.1 is an `insta` snapshot of the crate's own serialisation. | Why it matters: there is **zero** verification, at any level, of any of the four LiteLLM-specific wire shapes that are the entire justification for this crate existing (§1.1 rationale #1). If `metadata.tags` or body-`num_retries` is wrong, the headline feature is a silent no-op in production, every test stays green, and the only workaround is a new release. | Suggested fix: (a) resolve §16 Q3 and the `tags` shape against a live proxy **before** GATE 1, not "at implementation time" — they are load-bearing decisions, not implementation details; and (b) remove `tags`, `num_retries`, and `metadata` from the reserved set so `extra_body` is a genuine escape hatch (document last-writer-wins, or merge caller keys *under* provider keys inside `metadata`); or (c) ship `.tags_top_level(bool)` and a header-mode toggle for `num_retries` so both alternatives are reachable without a release.

### MAJOR

- **§7 / §11 / D3 — "The capability flag informs the agent loop" is false in this codebase** — grepping `\.capabilities\(\)` across `crates/` returns only the provider crates themselves, `runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs` (pure forwarding on the decorator), and `cli/src/model.rs`. `paigasus-helikon-core` never calls it; there is no consumer in the agent loop. | Why it matters: §7 uses this claim to justify not sending `parallel_tool_calls` ("The capability flag informs the agent loop; it does not go on the wire"), and D3's whole conservative-defaults posture rests on the flags being acted upon. Both arguments evaporate. It also weakens §1.1 rationale #3 — a misleading `KNOWN_MODELS` hit can't mislead a loop that never reads it. | Suggested fix: restate D3/§11 honestly — capabilities are advisory metadata for application code and traces — and drop or re-argue §1.1 #3 (see below).

- **§1.1 rationale #3 is wrong as written** — "no table can be correct, and the OpenAI crate's `KNOWN_MODELS` lookup is actively misleading when pointed at a proxy." `capabilities::lookup` (`openai/src/capabilities.rs:154-160`) falls through to `conservative_defaults()` for unknown ids, and that function's doc comment (`:24-33`) explicitly names LiteLLM. The only failure mode is an operator alias that *collides* with a table id, and `OpenAiModelBuilder::with_capabilities` (`openai/src/builder.rs:97`) already overrides it — which is exactly what D3 proposes. | Why it matters: this is one third of the crate's stated justification and it does not survive a read of the code it criticises. Rationales #1 and #2 do hold (I verified the closed `FinishReason` enum at `openai/src/backend/chat.rs:264-274`). | Suggested fix: delete #3 or downgrade it to a footnote, and promote the genuinely correct third argument the spec buries in §9: `reasoning_content` has no representation in async-openai's stream delta types, so reasoning streaming through a proxy is *structurally impossible* via the OpenAI crate. Also note that SMA-451 mandates a crate, so §1.1's job is to justify the crate's *shape*, not its existence.

- **§10 — rows 2 and 6 contradict each other on connect-refused** — row 2 maps "HTTP 502/503/504, **or connect-refused**" → `Unavailable`; row 6 maps "`reqwest` transport failure" → `Transport(String)`. A connection refusal *is* a reqwest transport failure. | Why it matters: two engineers build two different error surfaces from the same table. Both variants are retryable (`runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:80-85`), so the bug is invisible in retry behaviour and visible only in what the user sees. | Suggested fix: delete "or connect-refused" from row 2. Gemini already settled this — `gemini/src/model.rs:118` yields `ModelError::Transport(e.to_string())` for send failures.

- **§10 — HTTP 500 is missing, making transient proxy failures non-retryable** — the table jumps from 429 to "502/503/504". Gemini maps `500 | 502 | 503 | 504 → Unavailable` (`gemini/src/error.rs:17`). LiteLLM returns 500 for `litellm.InternalServerError` and for many upstream failures. Under this spec 500 lands in `Other(anyhow)`, which `RetryPolicy::is_retryable` (`runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:80-85`) explicitly excludes. | Why it matters: a wrapped `RetryingModel` will not retry the single most common transient proxy failure, and the workspace's two REST providers will disagree about what a 500 means. | Suggested fix: add 500 to the `Unavailable` row; decide explicitly on 408 and 529.

- **§10 — the `context_length_exceeded` code match is too narrow for LiteLLM specifically** — the table checks `error.code == "context_length_exceeded"` (OpenAI's spelling) before falling back to a substring match. LiteLLM's mapped exception is `ContextWindowExceededError` and it commonly emits `context_window_exceeded`. | Why it matters: §10 explicitly argues the structured code is "the primary signal" and the substring match is "the fragile fallback" — but on LiteLLM the primary signal misses and every context overflow takes the fragile path, on the one provider whose error strings are prefixed and rewritten (`litellm.BadRequestError: …`). | Suggested fix: match `context_window_exceeded` and `context_length_exceeded` on both `error.code` and `error.type`.

- **§10 — 429 on LiteLLM is not always a rate limit** — budget/quota exhaustion (`ExceededBudget`, "Budget has been exceeded", virtual-key max-budget) also returns 429. | Why it matters: mapping it to `RateLimited` makes a wrapped `RetryingModel` burn its full attempt budget — honouring `Retry-After` sleeps — against a hard limit that will never clear. | Suggested fix: inspect `error.type`/`error.code` for a budget signal before the 429 → `RateLimited` default, and map budget exhaustion to `Refused { reason }` (non-retryable).

- **§7.1 — the reserved-key rejection is incoherent as justified, and impossible at the stated time** — the rationale is "we never let a caller's key override a field the provider computed **per-request**", but the check runs at `build()`, before any `ModelRequest` exists. Whether `tools`, `tool_choice`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `top_p`, and `max_tokens` appear at all is a per-request decision (§7 says each is "only when … is Some"). So the rejection is necessarily unconditional: `.extra_body(json!({"temperature": 0.2}))` fails at build even when no request would ever have set `temperature`. | Why it matters: the mechanism is stricter than its own justification and the spec doesn't acknowledge it, so an implementer may "fix" it by moving the check to request time and get a different, unspecified API. | Suggested fix: pick one and state it — either "unconditional, for determinism and a build-time error" (and delete the per-request wording), or move the collision check into request assembly and surface it as a `ModelError`. Separately, `.metadata("tags", …)` should fail as a distinct `BuildError::ReservedMetadataKey(String)`, not `ReservedExtraBodyKey` — the name lies about which builder method was misused.

- **§5 / §7 — `metadata` values are `String`-only, and the wire isn't** — `metadata(key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>)` cannot express LiteLLM's nested metadata (`spend_logs_metadata`, Langfuse `session_id`/`generation_name`, numeric values) — and because `metadata` is a reserved `extra_body` key there is no workaround at all. | Why it matters: D4 names "metadata/tags fit the repo's existing Langfuse observability story" as a justification for the crate, but the API is strictly less expressive than the field it exists to expose. (Note also that the repo's Langfuse story is OTLP-based — `crates/paigasus-helikon/examples/langfuse_tracing.rs` — and unrelated to LiteLLM request metadata; the claim is loose.) | Suggested fix: `metadata(key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<serde_json::Value>)`, and/or drop `metadata` from the reserved set with caller keys merged beneath the provider's.

- **§9 — multi-choice (`n > 1`) is unhandled and `n` is not reserved** — `choices: Vec<Choice>` with no rule for which index to honour. `n` is absent from §7.1's reserved set, so `.extra_body(json!({"n": 2}))` is legal. The obvious implementation is the OpenAI provider's `for choice in &chunk.choices` (`openai/src/backend/chat.rs:246`), which interleaves two independent completions into one `TokenDelta` stream and emits two `Finish` events. Gemini specced this explicitly ("Only `candidates[0]` is read; `candidates[1..]` are intentionally ignored"). | Why it matters: corrupted assistant text with no error, and a second `Finish` after the terminal one. | Suggested fix: honour only the first choice (or `index == 0`), document it in the crate docs, and add `n` to the reserved set.

- **§9 — no rule for a truncated stream (EOF with no `finish_reason`)** — the mapping table has no row for it. `ModelTurnAccumulator` initialises `finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop` (`core/src/model.rs:558`), so a stream that ends without `Finish` yields an apparently-successful `Stop` turn; a stream that fabricates `Finish::Stop` is worse. Gemini specified this and tested it (`gemini/src/stream.rs:73-76`, `gemini/tests/gemini_streaming.rs:60` `truncated_stream_no_finish`). | Why it matters: a proxy dropping the connection mid-generation is indistinguishable from a clean completion; the truncated text is committed to session history as final. | Suggested fix: state "emit `Finish` only when a `finish_reason` was observed; on premature EOF end the stream without `Finish`" and add the test.

- **§6.1 — base-URL normalisation is lossy, irreversible, and its algorithm is unspecified** — three separate problems. (1) The trailing-`/v1` strip is unconditional with no override, so a gateway genuinely mounted under a path ending in `v1` is unreachable and there is no `.endpoint_path()`/`.chat_completions_path()` escape. (2) The spec describes string operations ("trim a trailing `/`, strip a trailing `/v1`, then append") but validates with `reqwest::Url::parse` — if the ops are string-level, `http://gw/litellm?key=x` becomes `http://gw/litellm?key=x/v1/chat/completions`. (3) `Url::parse` will not catch the most likely typo: `Url::parse("localhost:4000")` **succeeds** (scheme `localhost`, path `4000`), so `InvalidBaseUrl` gives false confidence. | Why it matters: D7 argues a build error beats silently targeting the wrong endpoint — but as specified, the validation admits the classic scheme-less typo and the normalisation can silently mangle a legitimate URL. | Suggested fix: normalise via `Url` (`path_segments_mut`), reject schemes other than `http`/`https` and reject a non-empty query or fragment, and add an explicit path override for gateways the heuristic gets wrong.

- **§12.2 — the "`Authorization` absent" test as specified passes against a broken implementation** — wiremock has no negative header matcher; a `Mock::given(method("POST"))` with no header condition matches whether or not the header was sent. The only correct form is capturing `server.received_requests().await` and asserting the key is absent from the recorded request. | Why it matters: this is the *security-relevant* assertion for D8 (optional auth), and as written it is vacuous. It is precisely the failure mode called out in this repo's own review history: a security test that would pass against vulnerable code. | Suggested fix: specify the `received_requests()` form, and mutation-check it — temporarily emit the header and confirm the test fails.

- **D6 / §15 R1 — the stated mitigation cannot detect the risk it claims to mitigate, and the duplication is under-counted** — R1 says drift is caught because "snapshot tests pin **this crate's** shape so drift is visible". A snapshot of crate B tells you nothing about crate A; both suites stay green while the two mappings diverge arbitrarily. And D6 accounts only for `to_chat_messages` (~120 lines, `openai/src/translate/request.rs:26-243`); the real copy is that plus `ChatTranslator` (~170 lines, `backend/chat.rs:196-375`), `translate_tool_choice` (`:181-194`), and `to_openai_response_format`. Meanwhile D6's stated cost of the alternative — "the same-PR core/facade bump ritual" — is a ~5-line Cargo.toml edit that CLAUDE.md documents step by step, and its second rationale ("the two mappings should be free to diverge") is close to self-refuting: LiteLLM's chat surface *is* the OpenAI Chat surface; divergence means LiteLLM stopped being OpenAI-compatible. | Why it matters: ~350 lines of subtle, already-battle-tested logic get re-derived without tests carried over, justified by a cost that is trivial and a benefit that is hypothetical. | Suggested fix: either hoist to `paigasus_helikon_core::wire::openai_chat` and pay the documented core+facade bump, or keep the copy and (a) port the OpenAI crate's unit tests verbatim alongside the copied functions so behavioural parity is pinned at copy time, and (b) add a real cross-crate parity test (facade test dir, both features on, shared fixture set asserted byte-identical). Update R1 to say which.

- **D5 — throwing away `x-litellm-*` leaves the crate with no correlation story, and the justification only covers half the problem** — D5 is correct that `ModelEvent` has no header carrier (verified: `core/src/model.rs:168-224`). But nothing prevents the provider from `tracing::debug!`-ing `x-litellm-call-id` / `x-litellm-model-id` on response receipt and attaching them to `ModelError::Other`'s anyhow context on failure. | Why it matters: this is a provider whose entire purpose is being a routing and observability chokepoint. As specified, a user with a failing call has no way to find it in LiteLLM's own logs — and §15 already accepts that capability mis-declaration and fallback surprises "surface as an upstream 400 mapped to `Other`", which is exactly the error the call-id would explain. Zero core change required. | Suggested fix: log the correlation headers at `debug` and include `x-litellm-call-id` in the error context for every non-2xx path. Narrow D5 to "not surfaced as a typed API".

- **§13 / packaging — the release-plz mechanism cited is the wrong one** — §13 says "release-plz's `dependencies_update` cascade handles the facade on its own." That cascade fires only when release-plz *itself* bumps a sibling. Here the new crate is authored at `0.1.0` by the PR, so release-plz never bumps it — this is exactly the "same-PR manual bump silently defeats `dependencies_update`" case CLAUDE.md documents. The facade gets bumped only by **path attribution** on the squashed commit touching `crates/paigasus-helikon/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`, which requires the squashed PR title to be `feat`/`fix`. | Why it matters: a `chore(...)`-titled squash merge would publish the new crate and leave the facade at `0.5.3` with no `litellm` feature — the exact drift that needed follow-up PR #50 after SMA-346. | Suggested fix: replace the claim with the Gemini spec's correct wording (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-sma-449-gemini-provider-design.md:433-436` — dependency-ordered publish, new crate depends only on already-published core, first publish is clean), and add an explicit constraint that the PR title must be `feat(providers): …`.

- **Packaging — the commit/PR-title scope is unspecified and the obvious guess breaks CI** — `providers-litellm` is absent from `.versionrc:18` (`scopeRegex`) and from `pr-title.yml:43-75` (`scopes`), as are `providers-gemini` and `providers-bedrock`. `feat(providers-litellm): …` is rejected by the local `commit-msg` hook and by the `commits` job. Because `pr-title.yml` runs on `pull_request_target`, the allowlist is read from `main`, so this PR cannot register a new scope and then use it in its own title. | Why it matters: a guaranteed red required check, discovered at push time, on a spec that otherwise documents CI conventions carefully. | Suggested fix: state that all commits and the PR title use scope `providers` (or `facade` for the wiring commit), and note the `pull_request_target` reason so nobody "fixes" it by editing the allowlist.

### MINOR

- **§14 — the documentation plan under-counts the pages that go stale.** `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md` says "Four adapters ship today" at **line 6 and again at line 85**, has a "Switching providers is one line" code block at **305-317** and an "Enabling the providers" toml at **334-343** — all four need editing. `docs/book/src/getting-started/workspace-layout.md:56-57` carries the crate list and is **not mentioned at all** in §14. `docs/book/src/reference/crates.md` needs *two* rows (roster ~line 27 **and** the feature→module map ~line 57), not one. Root `README.md:29` and `:38` both enumerate providers. Fix: enumerate these explicitly so nothing is skipped.

- **§11 — `.with_capabilities()` can produce a self-contradictory model.** An operator passing `ModelCapabilities::empty().with_tools()` sets `streaming: false` on a provider that has no non-streaming path (§3 out-of-scope: "The provider always streams"). Fix: force `streaming = true` after applying the override, or document that `streaming` is ignored.

- **§11 vs §8/§9/§12.1 — the default capability set contradicts the implemented feature set.** `conservative_defaults()` sets only `streaming|tools`, yet the crate emits `ReasoningDelta` (§9), maps `response_format` (§8), and snapshots an inline image part (§12.1) — so `reasoning`, `structured_output`, and `vision` are all `false` while implemented. §9's flourish ("this provider gets reasoning streaming that the Gemini provider still lacks") reads as contradicting §11. Fix: state explicitly that the flags describe the *unknown proxied backend*, not the translator's ability.

- **§5 / D7 — env var names are uncited and have no fallback.** `LITELLM_API_BASE` / `LITELLM_API_KEY` are asserted with no source; LiteLLM's own client conventions also use `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE` / `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY`. D7's "a loud build error beats silently targeting localhost" argument depends on operators having exported the exact name this crate expects. Gemini set the precedent for a documented fallback chain (`gemini/src/model.rs:46-48`). Fix: cite the source or add the `LITELLM_PROXY_*` fallback.

- **D8 / §6.2 — empty/whitespace API key is unhandled.** `.api_key("")` yields `Authorization: Bearer ` — a malformed header reqwest will happily send and LiteLLM will 401 on, which D8's "loud 401" framing then misattributes to a misconfigured *deployment*. Gemini has an explicit `EmptyApiKey`. Fix: treat empty/whitespace as absent, or add the variant.

- **§7/§8 — `ToolChoice::Required` / `Tool { name }` with empty `request.tools` is silently dropped.** §7 sends `tool_choice` "only when `ModelSettings.tool_choice` is `Some` AND `request.tools` is non-empty". The caller who set `Required` believes a tool call is guaranteed. Gemini errors on this case. Fix: at minimum `tracing::warn!`; ideally mirror Gemini and error.

- **§7 — the `drop_params` argument is applied to `parallel_tool_calls` but not to `max_tokens`.** §7 declines to send `parallel_tool_calls: false` because "LiteLLM only strips unknown params when the operator sets `drop_params`" — then unconditionally sends `max_tokens`, which OpenAI's o-series and gpt-5 reject in favour of `max_completion_tokens`, hitting exactly the same failure mode. Fix: state the decision explicitly (send `max_tokens`, or branch, or document the `drop_params` requirement) so the reasoning is consistent across adjacent fields.

- **§5 — no `Send`/`'static` story for the model's state.** §5 shows a bare `pub struct LiteLlmModel { /* … */ }`; `Model::invoke` returns `BoxStream<'static, …>` (`core/src/model.rs:72`), so the config must be cloned into the stream. Gemini solves it with `GeminiModel(Arc<Config>)` + `#[derive(Clone)]` (`gemini/src/model.rs:22-23`) precisely for this reason. Fix: state the `Arc<Config>` shape.

- **No timeout policy and no secret-redaction policy.** `reqwest::Client::new()` has no default timeout, so a hung self-hosted proxy hangs `invoke` indefinitely with cancellation as the only out — a higher-probability failure for an operator-run gateway than for a hyperscaler. Separately, if `Config`/`Builder` derive `Debug` with the key inline (as Gemini's `Auth::ApiKey(String)` does), `{model:?}` leaks the key; `extra_body` is arbitrary caller JSON that the §12.1 snapshots serialise wholesale. Fix: specify a `connect_timeout` default (or document that callers must supply `.http_client()`), a manual redacting `Debug`, and that no `tracing` event logs the `Authorization` header or a full request body.

- **§16 Q1 is already answered in-tree.** "Confirm `eventsource-stream` yields `[DONE]` as an ordinary `data` event" — `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/model.rs:155` does `if event.data == "[DONE]" { … return; }` and ships. Fix: cite the precedent and remove Q1 from the open list.

- **§12.4 "cancel mid-stream" is close to untestable with the stated harness.** Wiremock serves the whole body in one `set_body_raw` — the header comment on `openai/tests/chat_streaming.rs:3` says so outright ("Wiremock serves the entire fixture as one buffer — these tests prove byte-level correctness of the translator's state machine, not pacing"). The OpenAI crate only tests cancel-*before*-first-chunk (`tests/cancellation.rs:22`). Fix: either drop the mid-stream case or specify the mechanism (`set_delay` plus a multi-response mock sequence).

- **Missing tests for stated invariants.** No test that `parallel_tool_calls` is absent from the body (§7 invariant); no test that `previous_response_id` is never sent (§7); no test that the reserved-key set is *exhaustive* with respect to the serialiser. Fix: add a test that iterates the `RESERVED` const against a maximally-populated request body and asserts every emitted top-level key is reserved — this is the test that catches "we added `seed` to the body and forgot to reserve it".

- **§13 — no crates.io name preflight.** The Gemini spec carried a name-claim AC. Note that per this repo's history the crates.io API 403s the default curl User-Agent, so a naive availability check reads as unavailable. Fix: preflight `paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm` with a custom UA before GATE 1.

### QUESTIONS

- Is `classify()` a pure function taking `(status, code, type, message, retry_after_ms)`, as Gemini's is (`gemini/src/error.rs:9`)? §12.5's "one error-mapping test per row" is only cheap if it is; §10 never says.
- Do errors surface as `Err` returned from `invoke`, or as the first `Err` item on the returned stream? Gemini does the latter (`gemini/src/model.rs:136`); D8's "loud 401 → `ModelError::Refused` on first invoke" reads like the former. `RetryingModel` handles both (`runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:190`, `:234`), but call-site code differs.
- What happens to an SSE frame that fails to deserialise — warn-and-continue (Gemini) or terminate? And what happens to an `error` frame that arrives *after* a `Finish` has been emitted?
- Is `delta.reasoning_content` the only reasoning field? Some LiteLLM builds emit `delta.reasoning` and/or `delta.thinking_blocks` depending on backend and version. Does §9 want a fallback chain, and does the answer change the `ReasoningDelta` mapping?
- What is the documented interaction between LiteLLM's server-side `num_retries`/`fallbacks` and a client-side `RetryingModel`? Attempts multiply (N_client × N_server) and each client retry re-runs the entire fallback chain, so a `RetryPolicy::new()` (3 attempts) around `.num_retries(2)` plus two fallbacks is up to 18 upstream calls per turn. Should the crate docs warn, or should `.num_retries()` be documented as mutually exclusive with `RetryingModel`?
- Is there an empty-conversation guard? OpenAI Chat 400s on `messages: []`, and Gemini specced an explicit early `ModelError` for it. Is "let it 400 upstream" the deliberate choice here?
- Does `Usage` really arrive exactly once? §9 asserts "One terminal snapshot satisfies core's cumulative-within-turn / last-wins contract trivially" — but several LiteLLM backends emit per-chunk usage. Last-wins still holds if the values are cumulative; it breaks if any backend emits per-chunk *deltas* (`core/src/model.rs:198-204` says such a provider would under-count). Has this been checked?

## What's good

- **§1.1 is genuinely rigorous** and rare: it starts by arguing against its own existence, names the exact prior art with a file:line, and two of its three arguments survive verification — the closed `FinishReason` enum is real (`openai/src/backend/chat.rs:264-274`, with the code's own comment noting the enum is not `#[non_exhaustive]`), and `base_url()`'s LiteLLM doc comment is exactly where the spec says it is (`openai/src/builder.rs:72`). Keep this section's posture; just fix rationale #3.
- **Every field of `ModelSettings` is accounted for**, including an explicit and correct decision on `previous_response_id` (§7) — checked against `core/src/model.rs:134-154`. Provider specs routinely leave a field unmapped and undiscussed; this one doesn't.
- **Dependency hygiene is exact.** Every crate listed in §13 exists in root `[workspace.dependencies]` at the right feature set, matching `providers-gemini/Cargo.toml:17-38` line for line, and **no new third-party crate is introduced** — so no new licence, advisory, or rustls-`CryptoProvider` surface. Together with the `.gitattributes` rule, the facade `///`-on-`pub use` note, and the `-D warnings` docs-job note, this shows CLAUDE.md was read rather than skimmed.
- **D9's instinct — never silently drop a caller's key — is right**, even though the mechanism needs rework. Preserve the principle when reworking §7.1.
Thorough critique. Before folding anything in, let me verify its highest-impact claims myself.

- **Gemini already implements the exact deferred-`finish()` + warn-and-continue pattern** the challenger prescribes (`gemini/src/stream.rs:73`, `model.rs:155-169`) ✅.
